data.title: We Think Shareholders Should Be Aware Of Some Factors Beyond Furukawa Electric's (TSE:5801) Profit
data.description:
Furukawa Electric Co., Ltd.'s (TSE:5801) stock rose after it released a robust earnings report. Despite the strong profit numbers, we believe that there are some deeper issues which investors should look into.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against Furukawa Electric's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Furukawa Electric has an accrual ratio of 0.22 for the year to September 2026. We can therefore deduce that its free cash flow fell well short of covering its statutory profit. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of JP¥32b despite its profit of JP¥118.3b, mentioned above. We saw that FCF was JP¥11b a year ago though, so Furukawa Electric has at least been able to generate positive FCF in the past. Having said that, there is more to the story. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

Check out our latest analysis for Furukawa Electric

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Given the accrual ratio, it's not overly surprising that Furukawa Electric's profit was boosted by unusual items worth JP¥48b in the last twelve months. We can't deny that higher profits generally leave us optimistic, but we'd prefer it if the profit were to be sustainable. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. We can see that Furukawa Electric's positive unusual items were quite significant relative to its profit in the year to September 2026. As a result, we can surmise that the unusual items are making its statutory profit significantly stronger than it would otherwise be.

Our Take On Furukawa Electric's Profit Performance

Summing up, Furukawa Electric received a nice boost to profit from unusual items, but could not match its paper profit with free cash flow. For the reasons mentioned above, we think that a perfunctory glance at Furukawa Electric's statutory profits might make it look better than it really is on an underlying level. Keep in mind, when it comes to analysing a stock it's worth noting the risks involved. You'd be interested to know, that we found 3 warning signs for Furukawa Electric and you'll want to know about these.

data.title: What Investors Got Wrong About MINISO Group Before The Drop
data.description:
MINISO Group’s latest numbers read like progress, yet the shareholder experience over the same spell looks very different. Investors who held MINISO Group over the past year are down 46.6%, including dividends. If you had been weighing an entry in November 2025, you would have seen upbeat analyst arguments, brisk revenue growth, and growing IP ambitions. The Two MINISO Group Stories Investors Were Weighing

The shares cost US$19.59 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at MINISO Group then had two clear stories to choose between.

The bullish narrative put Fair Value at US$26.6, 36% above the start price. This view was based on the idea that international expansion and proprietary IP could support higher margins, as analysts assumed profit margins might rise from 13.9% to 16.4%.

The bearish view set Fair Value at US$16.5, 16% below the start price. This view stressed the risk that rising online shopping and higher logistics and labor costs could pressure margins, and analysts expected margins to edge down from 13.9% to 13.7%.

What The Results Changed For The MINISO Group Story

The most direct test of the bullish MINISO Group thesis came from Q3 2026 results. Revenue reached CNY 6,625.298m versus CNY 5,796.645m a year earlier, which supported the growth side of the upbeat case. Net income fell from CNY 440.539m to CNY 283.216m and net margin moved from 7.6% to 4.3%, which challenged the expected margin uplift. Overall, the evidence pointed in both directions.

The key assumption here was that higher sales would translate into stronger profitability. When you assess another retailer, test that link yourself by tracking net income and net margin next to revenue whenever strong top line figures are used to justify optimism.

What Today’s MINISO Price Asks You To Believe

MINISO Group now trades at US$10.22, with this Narrative’s Fair Value sitting above that level according to Bejgal, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative. The focus is squarely on global store openings, larger “super stores,” and IP driven product lines to support the business case.

If you look at the recent fall as a potential opening rather than a warning, you would need to believe MINISO can keep scaling that store rollout, super store format, and IP collaboration model without eroding profitability.

"MINISO is well-positioned to benefit from several key industry tailwinds: Global Demand for Value and Aesthetics: In the current global economic climate, consumers are increasingly seeking value for money. MINISO's core value proposition of offering well-designed, high-quality, and affordable lifestyle products directly meets this need."

Every purchase, membership and loyalty perk relies on dense digital plumbing. You feel it as fast checkout, tailored offers and flexible payment options.

Its services help retailers test ideas quickly, handle surges and plug in new digital tools. As commerce leans harder on that stack, the role this group plays could quietly shift in influence.

data.title: We Don’t Think MAKUS' (KOSDAQ:093520) Earnings Should Make Shareholders Too Comfortable
data.description:
Solid profit numbers didn't seem to be enough to please MAKUS Inc.'s (KOSDAQ:093520) shareholders. Our analysis has found some concerning factors which weaken the profit's foundation.

A Closer Look At MAKUS' Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

MAKUS has an accrual ratio of 1.33 for the year to September 2026. Statistically speaking, that's a real negative for future earnings. To wit, the company did not generate one whit of free cashflow in that time. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of ₩26b despite its profit of ₩35.1b, mentioned above. We saw that FCF was ₩85b a year ago though, so MAKUS has at least been able to generate positive FCF in the past. Having said that, there is more to the story. The accrual ratio is reflecting the impact of unusual items on statutory profit, at least in part. The good news for shareholders is that MAKUS' accrual ratio was much better last year, so this year's poor reading might simply be a case of a short term mismatch between profit and FCF. Shareholders should look for improved cashflow relative to profit in the current year, if that is indeed the case.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

The fact that the company had unusual items boosting profit by ₩6.0b, in the last year, probably goes some way to explain why its accrual ratio was so weak. While it's always nice to have higher profit, a large contribution from unusual items sometimes dampens our enthusiasm. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And that's as you'd expect, given these boosts are described as 'unusual'. Assuming those unusual items don't show up again in the current year, we'd thus expect profit to be weaker next year (in the absence of business growth, that is).

Our Take On MAKUS' Profit Performance

Summing up, MAKUS received a nice boost to profit from unusual items, but could not match its paper profit with free cash flow. Considering all this we'd argue MAKUS' profits probably give an overly generous impression of its sustainable level of profitability. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, SAXA recorded an accrual ratio of 0.78. As a general rule, that bodes poorly for future profitability. To wit, the company did not generate one whit of free cashflow in that time. Over the last year it actually had negative free cash flow of JP¥635m, in contrast to the aforementioned profit of JP¥16.2b. We saw that FCF was JP¥3.0b a year ago though, so SAXA has at least been able to generate positive FCF in the past. Having said that, there is more to the story. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

View our latest analysis for SAXA

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

Given the accrual ratio, it's not overly surprising that SAXA's profit was boosted by unusual items worth JP¥22b in the last twelve months. We can't deny that higher profits generally leave us optimistic, but we'd prefer it if the profit were to be sustainable. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. SAXA had a rather significant contribution from unusual items relative to its profit to September 2026. All else being equal, this would likely have the effect of making the statutory profit a poor guide to underlying earnings power.

Our Take On SAXA's Profit Performance

Summing up, SAXA received a nice boost to profit from unusual items, but could not match its paper profit with free cash flow. For all the reasons mentioned above, we think that, at a glance, SAXA's statutory profits could be considered to be low quality, because they are likely to give investors an overly positive impression of the company. Keep in mind, when it comes to analysing a stock it's worth noting the risks involved. For example, we've found that SAXA has 3 warning signs (2 can't be ignored!) that deserve your attention before going any further with your analysis.

In this article we've looked at a number of factors that can impair the utility of profit numbers, and we've come away cautious. But there is always more to discover if you are capable of focussing your mind on minutiae. Some people consider a high return on equity to be a good sign of a quality business. data.title: We Ran A Stock Scan For Earnings Growth And KIMURA KOHKILtd (TSE:6231) Passed With Ease
data.description:
The excitement of investing in a company that can reverse its fortunes is a big draw for some speculators, so even companies that have no revenue, no profit, and a record of falling short, can manage to find investors. But as Peter Lynch said in One Up On Wall Street, 'Long shots almost never pay off.' A loss-making company is yet to prove itself with profit, and eventually the inflow of external capital may dry up.

In contrast to all that, many investors prefer to focus on companies like KIMURA KOHKILtd (TSE:6231), which has not only revenues, but also profits. Even if this company is fairly valued by the market, investors would agree that generating consistent profits will continue to provide KIMURA KOHKILtd with the means to add long-term value to shareholders.

How Quickly Is KIMURA KOHKILtd Increasing Earnings Per Share?

Generally, companies experiencing growth in earnings per share (EPS) should see similar trends in share price. That makes EPS growth an attractive quality for any company. Shareholders will be happy to know that KIMURA KOHKILtd's EPS has grown 29% each year, compound, over three years. If growth like this continues on into the future, then shareholders will have plenty to smile about.

Top-line growth is a great indicator that growth is sustainable, and combined with a high earnings before interest and taxation (EBIT) margin, it's a great way for a company to maintain a competitive advantage in the market. EBIT margins for KIMURA KOHKILtd remained fairly unchanged over the last year, however the company should be pleased to report its revenue growth for the period of 17% to JP¥20b. That's encouraging news for the company!

KIMURA KOHKILtd isn't a huge company, given its market capitalisation of JP¥30b. That makes it extra important to check on its balance sheet strength.

Are KIMURA KOHKILtd Insiders Aligned With All Shareholders?

It's pleasing to see company leaders with putting their money on the line, so to speak, because it increases alignment of incentives between the people running the business, and its true owners. So it is good to see that KIMURA KOHKILtd insiders have a significant amount of capital invested in the stock. Indeed, they hold JP¥6.3b worth of its stock. That's a lot of money, and no small incentive to work hard. Those holdings account for over 21% of the company; visible skin in the game.

Is KIMURA KOHKILtd Worth Keeping An Eye On?

If you believe that share price follows earnings per share you should definitely be delving further into KIMURA KOHKILtd's strong EPS growth. Further, the high level of insider ownership is impressive and suggests that the management appreciates the EPS growth and has faith in KIMURA KOHKILtd's continuing strength. Fast growth and confident insiders should be enough to warrant further research, so it would seem that it's a good stock to follow.
